page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal server equipped with Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors delivering 288 vCPUs across 144 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Clocked at up to 4.2 GHz, the system includes 504 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance is paired with 1080 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing a ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU, and integrates 19,326 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage across six drives.

Performance benchmarks show strong aggregate throughput across parallel computing and data-intensive tasks. In multi-core CPU testing, the server achieves top-tier scores in stress-ng multi-core evaluation and PassMark CPU metrics, including encryption, physics, and extended instruction benchmarks. Memory subsystem tests report uncached large-block read speeds exceeding 1,000 GB/s and write speeds reaching 428 GB/s. In-memory data structures perform at high velocity, recording 401.21 million Redis SET operations per second and high static web serving throughput.

The integration of substantial local NVMe capacity directly on bare metal eliminates hypervisor overhead and external storage latency. While single-threaded workloads reflect typical per-core performance tiers, the architecture is balanced for dense parallel operations. The combination of high core counts, hardware matrix accelerators, massive memory bandwidth, and 19.3 TB of local NVMe makes this server appropriate for high-throughput transactional and analytical databases, large-scale Redis caching, parallel compilation, and data transformation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd-metal is a dedicated bare-metal server powered by 144-core Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors delivering 288 vCPUs at up to 4.2 GHz. Supported by 504 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 extensions, the system is equipped with 1080 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 6 GHz and 19,326 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage across six drives. Benchmark results place the system in the top tier for multi-core stress testing, PassMark compute scores, memory bandwidth, and Redis operations, where it processes over 400 million operations per second. With 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU and direct NVMe access without virtualization overhead, the instance provides high resource density for high-throughput transactional databases, large in-memory caches, large software build farms, and parallel batch data processing.
